pr_title: ESQL: Fix Analyzer to not interpret escaped * as a pattern
pr_body:
Fix a bug in the Analyzer which always considered `*` (match any string)
 in field names even when escaped (back quoted). This caused the clause
 to be too greedy and either keep or drop too many fields.

Fix #104955

issue_context.title: ESQL: Inconsistent resolution message for unresolved fields
issue_context.body:
### Description

In some places, the Analyzer uses a different error message for unresolved attributes - instead of the "Cannot find x, did you mean [y,z,w]?" a basic "No match found for ..[]" is returned.
See [the pattern resolution](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/analysis/Analyzer.java#L589) vs the [regular one](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/analysis/Analyzer.java#L598).

This gets picked up when dealing with escaped wildcard:
```
FROM index
| STATS COUNT(*)
| SORT `count(*)`
```
 """Found 1 problem:
line x:y: No match found for [count(*)]"""

Thus there are two problems here:
- an escaped name containing * gets confused for a pattern (it's not)
- the escaped pattern doesn't match anything, see whether it makes sense to provide suggestions for it
comments:
A more severe use case:

```
row a = 5 | stats Count(*) by a | eval `Count(123)` = a * a | keep `Count(*)`

   Count(*)    |  Count(123)   
---------------+---------------
1              |25              
```

review_comments:
Most of the changes here are massaging the previous code to work without an `UnresolvedAttribute`.
A bool parameter was not used and the extension was done through a supplier in order to throw an error when the pattern does not match.

```suggestion
            msg += ", did you mean "
```

The message is slightly inconsistent with what we use in ql in general (`to match` is extra).
I've done the change on purpose to signal it's a pattern not regular name matching.
Specifically for this change, please add some tests in `IndexResolverFieldNamesTests`.
allowCompound just like `isPattern` were not needed.
Had to open the constructor up for the UnresolvedNamePattern.
